outputs.L1:
**(InStyle) —** After years in the bronze age, when sun-kissed cheeks and gloss reigned supreme, fall’s return to glamour signals a major comeback for lipstick. Lipstick outsold gloss by $76 million last year, and beauty companies are racing to introduce new formulas that are more wearable than ever.

So pucker up. We’ll show you how to apply lipstick perfectly and choose the most flattering shades for day and night. For foolproof application, stick to sheer, subdued shades in the morning, and save deep, bold colors—which require more time and precision—for evening.

## Daytime Equation

**1. Condition and protect.**  
Use a balm that contains sunscreen, such as Softlips Raspberry with Green Tea SPF 20. “Dab some on immediately after getting out of the shower, when your lips are still a little moist,” suggests Hollywood pro Kara Yoshimoto Bua. The smoother your lips, the more perfect your lipstick will look.

**2. Choose a soft shade.**  
Select a rose or nude that can be applied straight from the tube. A hydrating formula will ensure a smooth coat of color. Try Neutrogena Moistureshine Soothing Lipsheers in Fresh Rose.

**3. Blot, reapply, and blot again.**  
This removes excess oils and creates a stain, says Bua. “The color looks more natural and lasts longer.” Instead of tissues, use lint-free blotting papers, such as Boscia Fresh Blotting Linens ($10).

## Nighttime Equation

**1. Exfoliate.**  
Before applying a bold hue such as red or burgundy, remove dry patches with Sally Hansen Gentle Peel for Rough Lips ($10; at drugstores), which uses fruit enzymes.

**2. Create a base.**  
Apply a gel-based primer to fill in fine lines around the mouth and help lipstick glide on more smoothly. One to try: Olay Regenerist Lip Treatment ($19; at drugstores).

**3. Define your lips.**  
Outline the borders of your mouth with a pencil to prevent color from bleeding, says Robin Fredriksz, who created Barrymore’s deep fuchsia lip. To avoid an unnaturally dark outline, choose a shade lighter than your lipstick, such as Revlon ColorStay Lip Liner in Plum ($8; at drugstores).

**4. Brush on color.**  
For greater control, apply lipstick with a brush. Try the Shu Uemura Kolinsky Portable Extra Lip Brush ($35) with IsaDora Perfect Moisture Lipstick in Bordeaux Red ($11).

## Makeup Artists’ Favorites

Like the rest of us, cosmetics professionals return to the same lipsticks again and again. From the just-right daytime rose to the classic evening red, here are some of their all-time favorite picks for day and night.

### Carmindy

Carmindy’s neutral daytime picks are designed to “enhance your natural lip color.” For evening, she recommends dark berry or true red for all skin tones.

**Her clients:** Heidi Klum and Jamie-Lynn Sigler.  
**Day shades:** Benefit Silky Finish in Candy Store, $16; Givenchy Rouge Interdit in Secret Pink, $26.  
**Night colors:** Nars in Scarlet Empress, $23; Revlon Super Lustrous in Love That Red, $8, at drugstores.

### AJ Crimson

AJ Crimson favors subtle pink or sheer beige for all skin tones during the day. For evening, he recommends bright red for fair complexions and deep purple for darker ones.

**His clients:** Missy Elliott and Amerie.  
**Day shades:** Chanel Rouge Hydrabase in Pink Sugar, $25; Laura Mercier in Candy Pink, $22.  
**Night colors:** Maybelline Moisture Extreme in Royal Red, $7, at drugstores; MAC in Cyber, $14.

### Melissa Silver

For daytime, Melissa Silver uses fuchsia on cool skin tones and peachy nude on warm ones. For evening, she says, “Anyone can wear plum or sheer red.”

**Her clients:** Renée Zellweger and Cindy Crawford.  
**Day shades:** Clinique Colour Surge Butter Shine in Fresh Watermelon, $14; Lancôme Le Rouge Absolu in Nectariche, $25.  
**Night colors:** MAC in Spice It Up!, $14; Sonia Kashuk in Sheer Cherry Blossom, $8.

**(InStyle) —** For several years, beauty was dominated by bronzed skin, glowing cheeks and shiny gloss. Now that glamour is returning for fall, lipstick is back in a big way. Last year, lipstick sales exceeded those of lip gloss by $76 million, prompting cosmetics brands to compete with new, increasingly easy-to-wear formulas.

Get ready to perfect your pout: Here’s how to achieve flawless lipstick application and choose the best shades for both daytime and evening. For an easy morning look, opt for muted, translucent colors. Reserve rich, dramatic hues—which demand greater care and accuracy—for nighttime.

### The daytime formula

**1. Moisturize and shield your lips.**  
Apply a lip balm with sun protection, such as Softlips Raspberry with Green Tea SPF 20. Hollywood makeup professional Kara Yoshimoto Bua recommends putting it on as soon as you step out of the shower, while your lips remain slightly damp. The softer and smoother the surface, the better your lipstick will appear.

**2. Pick a gentle, wearable color.**  
Choose a nude or rose shade that can be swept on directly from the tube. A moisturizing lipstick will help the color glide on evenly. One option is Neutrogena Moistureshine Soothing Lipsheers in Fresh Rose.

**3. Blot twice.**  
Bua advises blotting after the first application, adding another layer and blotting once more. This removes extra oils and leaves behind a stain-like finish that looks more natural and stays in place longer. Rather than using tissue, try a lint-free product such as Boscia Fresh Blotting Linens ($10).

### The nighttime formula

**1. Smooth away dry skin.**  
Before wearing a strong shade such as burgundy or red, exfoliate your lips. Sally Hansen Gentle Peel for Rough Lips ($10 at drugstores) contains fruit enzymes that lift away flaky areas.

**2. Prepare the surface.**  
Use a gel primer to soften the appearance of fine lines around the lips and allow color to apply more evenly. Olay Regenerist Lip Treatment ($19 at drugstores) is one possibility.

**3. Outline carefully.**  
Makeup artist Robin Fredriksz, who created Barrymore’s deep-fuchsia lip look, recommends tracing the lip edges with pencil to stop the color from feathering. To prevent a harsh, overly dark border, select a liner lighter than the lipstick—for example, Revlon ColorStay Lip Liner in Plum ($8 at drugstores).

**4. Use a brush for precision.**  
Applying lipstick with a brush gives you greater control. Try the Shu Uemura Kolinsky Portable Extra Lip Brush ($35) paired with Isadora Perfect Moisture Lipstick in Bordeaux Red ($11).

### Makeup artists’ top choices

Professional makeup artists, like everyone else, repeatedly return to favorite lipsticks. Their reliable selections range from ideal daytime roses to timeless reds for evening.

#### Carmindy

For daytime, Carmindy chooses neutral colors intended to bring out the wearer’s own natural lip tone. After dark, she suggests either a true red or a deep berry shade for every complexion.

For daytime, Melissa Silver applies fuchsia to cool-toned complexions and peach-toned nude to warm skin. In the evening, she says that sheer red and plum work for anyone.

**Clients:** Renée Zellweger and Cindy Crawford

**Day:**

outputs.L4:
Lipstick is making a strong comeback, moving ahead of lip gloss as women embrace a more polished, glamorous look. In fact, lipstick outsold gloss by $76 million, suggesting that richer color and classic finishes are once again becoming beauty essentials. New formulas have also made lipstick easier to wear, offering improved comfort, smoother application, and longer-lasting color.

For daytime, the key is to keep the look soft and effortless. Begin by moisturizing the lips with a lightweight balm to prevent dryness and create an even surface. Once the balm has absorbed, apply a sheer lipstick or a softly tinted formula in a natural, wearable shade. The color can be dabbed on with a fingertip for a subtle stain or applied directly and blotted for a more refined finish. This routine adds freshness without looking overly formal.

Evening lipstick calls for more preparation, especially when wearing deep, bright, or highly pigmented colors. Start by gently exfoliating the lips to remove dry skin, then apply a small amount of balm. Follow with a lip primer to smooth the surface and help the color stay in place. Define the edges with a liner that matches the lipstick, correcting the shape carefully and filling in the lips if extra staying power is needed. Apply the lipstick in thin, even layers, blot between applications, and clean up the outline for a crisp, professional result.

The shift from gloss to lipstick reflects a broader return to glamour, but today’s look does not have to feel difficult or old-fashioned. With the right preparation, application techniques, and modern formulas, lipstick can appear smooth, precise, and polished while lasting comfortably throughout the day or night.

counterfactuals.prompt: How should I apply lipstick perfectly for day versus night? Include recommended products, shades, and advice from celebrity makeup artists.
counterfactuals.output:
## Start with a smooth base

1. **Exfoliate gently** with a damp washcloth or lip scrub—avoid scrubbing cracked lips.
2. Apply a thin layer of balm for 5–10 minutes, then **blot it off**. Excess balm makes lipstick slide.
3. If your lip line is uneven, tap a tiny amount of concealer around the perimeter—not over the whole lip.

Celebrity makeup artist **Lisa Eldridge** often emphasizes working in thin layers and refining the lip shape after the initial application rather than drawing a harsh outline immediately.

---

# Daytime lips: polished, soft, and easy to maintain

### Application

1. Choose a **rose, pinky nude, peach, caramel, or muted berry** close to your natural lip color.
2. Apply lipstick from the center outward, ideally with a finger or brush for a diffused finish.
3. Use a liner that matches **your lips or the lipstick**, then correct only where needed. Slightly overline the center of the upper and lower lips, but follow your natural line at the corners.
4. Blot once and reapply a thin layer.
5. For a fresher look, add balm or gloss only to the center.

This follows the softly enhanced approach associated with artists such as **Bobbi Brown**, who has long recommended choosing natural shades based on the underlying color of the lips, and **Charlotte Tilbury**, whose signature technique uses liner to subtly balance and define the shape.

### Day-shade guide

- **Fair/light skin:** rosy beige, soft pink, peach nude  
- **Medium/olive skin:** warm rose, caramel nude, terracotta pink  
- **Tan/deep skin:** toffee, cocoa rose, warm berry, brick nude  
- If a nude looks chalky, choose one with **more rose, caramel, or brown** and use a deeper liner.

### Recommended daytime products

- **Clinique Almost Lipstick — Black Honey:** sheer, adaptable berry
- **NARS Afterglow Sensual Shine Lipstick — Dolce Vita:** sheer dusty rose
- **Charlotte Tilbury Matte Revolution — Pillow Talk Medium:** defined rose-brown
- **MAC Matte Lipstick — Velvet Teddy:** beige-brown; best with a complementary liner
- **Fenty Beauty Gloss Bomb Cream — Fenty Glow:** warm rosy nude gloss
- **NYX Slim Lip Pencil:** affordable option with a broad nude-to-brown shade range
- **Maybelline Lifter Gloss — Stone or Topaz:** comfortable neutral glosses

**Best daytime finish:** satin, sheer, balm-like, or softly blotted matte.

---

# Nighttime lips: sculpted, saturated, and long-wearing

### Application

1. Prep and blot the lips thoroughly.
2. For maximum wear, cover the lips lightly with liner—not just the edges.
3. Apply lipstick with a **lip brush**, especially for red, wine, plum, or deep brown.
4. Blot through a single layer of tissue. For extra durability, lightly dust translucent powder over the tissue, then apply a second thin coat.
5. Clean the perimeter with a small flat brush and minimal concealer.
6. For dimension, place a slightly lighter lipstick or gloss at the center.

**Pat McGrath** is known for building bold lips in precise, layered applications, while **Mario Dedivanovic** frequently uses strategic liner and subtle tonal variation to create fuller-looking, balanced lips. Keep overlining restrained: focus on the cupid’s bow and center of the lower lip rather than extending the corners.

### Night-shade guide

- **Classic glamour:** true red or blue-red  
- **Warm, dramatic look:** brick, chili red, burnt orange  
- **Moody evening look:** wine, oxblood, blackberry, deep plum  
- **Modern neutral:** deep rose-brown, espresso, or chocolate  
- **Deep skin tones:** richly pigmented reds, burgundies, and browns generally retain more impact than pale or white-based colors.

### Recommended nighttime products

- **MAC Retro Matte Lipstick — Ruby Woo:** iconic blue-red matte
- **Fenty Beauty Stunna Lip Paint — Uncensored:** vivid universal-style red
- **Pat McGrath Labs MatteTrance Lipstick — Elson:** saturated blue-red
- **Lisa Eldridge True Velvet Lip Colour:** plush matte formula; choose a red, berry, or deeper neutral suited to your undertone
- **Dior Rouge Dior — 999:** classic red available in multiple finishes
- **Maybelline Super Stay Matte Ink — Pioneer:** affordable, very long-wearing red
- **NYX Shine Loud High Shine Lip Color:** long wear with a glossy topcoat

**Best nighttime finish:** precise matte or satin for longevity; lacquered gloss for drama, provided you do not mind touch-ups.

---

## Celebrity-artist tricks that make the biggest difference

- **Lisa Eldridge:** Use thin layers and inspect the lips from normal conversational distance; extreme close-up can encourage overcorrection.
- **Charlotte Tilbury:** Define the cupid’s bow and subtly round the upper lip for a fuller appearance.
- **Mario Dedivanovic:** Use a liner only slightly deeper than the lipstick, blending inward so there is no obvious ring.
- **Pat McGrath:** Layer pigment and perfect the edges with a brush for editorial-level intensity.
- **Sir John:** Balance a strong lip with fresh skin and controlled makeup elsewhere; a bold lip usually looks most modern without competing heavy features.

These are summaries of techniques commonly demonstrated or discussed by the artists, not claims that they personally endorse every product listed.

## Final checks

- **Prevent lipstick on teeth:** place a clean finger between your lips, close them around it, and pull it out.
- **Avoid feathering:** use liner, thin layers, and a clear lip pencil around the outer edge if necessary.
- **For mature or textured lips:** favor creamy matte or satin formulas over very dry liquid mattes.
- **Carry for touch-ups:** lipstick, liner, cotton swab, and a tiny concealer brush.
- With bold shades, check the result in **daylight and indoor lighting** before leaving.

# How to Take Your Lipstick From Subtle by Day to Bold by Night

A great lip look doesn’t have to stay the same from your morning coffee through evening cocktails. With a few strategic products—and the right application techniques—you can wear a soft, polished shade during the day, then transform it into a saturated statement lip after dark.

*Prices are approximate and may vary by retailer.*

## Daytime: The Soft, Blurred Lip

For daytime, makeup artists generally recommend choosing a shade close to your natural lip color. Think rosy nude, muted peach, soft mauve, or sheer berry. Lightweight textures and diffused edges keep the effect effortless.

### Step 1: Prep Without Overdoing It

Gently buff away dry skin with a damp washcloth, then apply a thin layer of balm. Let it absorb while you finish the rest of your makeup.

**Try:**  
- **Burt’s Bees Beeswax Lip Balm**, about **$5**  
- **Summer Fridays Lip Butter Balm**, about **$24**

**Expert tip:** Too much balm can cause lipstick to slide. Blot off any excess before adding color.

### Step 2: Neutralize Uneven Pigment

If your natural lip color is uneven, tap a tiny amount of concealer around the edges—not across the entire mouth. This creates a clean canvas while preserving dimension.

**Try:**  
- **e.l.f. Hydrating Camo Concealer**, about **$8**  
- **NARS Radiant Creamy Concealer**, about **$32**

### Step 3: Define With a Nude Pencil

Choose a liner that matches your lips rather than your lipstick. Trace the natural perimeter, then lightly shade the corners and Cupid’s bow. Blend inward with a fingertip.

**Try:**  
- **NYX Professional Makeup Slim Lip Pencil**, about **$5**  
- **Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat**, about **$25**

Makeup professionals often use this technique to create subtle definition without leaving behind an obvious outline as lipstick fades.

### Step 4: Press On Color

Instead of swiping lipstick directly from the tube, dab it onto the center of your lips and blend outward with your finger. The result should look softly stained rather than perfectly painted.

**Flattering daytime options:**  
- **Clinique Almost Lipstick in Black Honey**, about **$25**  
- **Revlon Super Lustrous Glass Shine Lipstick**, about **$12**  
- **Merit Signature Lip**, about **$26**

### Step 5: Add Strategic Shine

Tap clear balm or gloss onto the center of the lower lip. Keeping shine concentrated in one area makes lips appear fuller without looking overly glossy.

---

## Nighttime: The High-Impact Statement Lip

After dark, deepen the color and sharpen the shape. Classic red is always reliable, but burgundy, vivid fuchsia, brick, plum, and even deep chocolate can make just as much of an impact.

### Step 1: Remove the Day’s Leftovers

Wipe away your daytime lip color and balm with micellar water or a gentle makeup-removing cloth. Starting fresh prevents the new shade from becoming muddy.

**Try:**  
- **Garnier SkinActive Micellar Cleansing Water**, about **$11**

### Step 2: Create a Precise Outline

Use a sharpened pencil that matches your evening lipstick. Begin at the Cupid’s bow, define the center of the lower lip, and then connect the corners using short strokes.

For extra longevity, fill in the entire lip with pencil. This creates a base that helps color remain visible even after the top layer wears away.

**Try:**  
- **Make Up For Ever Artist Color Pencil**, about **$24**  
- **MAC Lip Pencil**, about **$25**

### Step 3: Apply Bold Color in Thin Layers

Use a lip brush for maximum control, especially with red or dark lipstick. Apply one thin coat, blot with a tissue, then add a second coat. Two light layers generally last longer and look smoother than one heavy application.

**Statement shades to consider:**  
- **Maybelline SuperStay Matte Ink Liquid Lipstick**, about **$11**  
- **Fenty Beauty Stunna Lip Paint**, about **$29**  
- **Dior Rouge Dior Lipstick**, about **$49**

### Step 4: Perfect the Edges

Run a small amount of concealer around the outside of the lips with a flat brush. Blend carefully so there’s no visible halo.

**Expert tip:** Correct only the areas that need it. A thick ring of concealer can make a bold lip look unnatural in photos.

### Step 5: Choose the Right Finish

For the most staying power, use a matte or satin formula. If you prefer a lacquered effect, place gloss only at the center of the mouth rather than covering the entire lip.

A deeper color can also feel more wearable when paired with softly defined eyes, groomed brows, and luminous skin. If you’re wearing dramatic eye makeup too, keep blush and contour restrained to maintain balance.

## The Fastest Day-to-Night Shortcut

No time to start over? Keep your daytime nude lipstick in place and layer a deeper liner over it. Blend the liner inward, then add a coordinating red, berry, or plum shade at the center. The nude base softens the bold pigment, creating a dimensional evening color in under two minutes.

Finish by blotting once, checking your teeth, and slipping the lipstick and liner into your bag for touch-ups.

counterfactuals.prompt: What lipstick colors do makeup artists Carmindy, AJ Crimson, and Melissa Silver recommend for different skin tones and occasions? Include their favorite products and application techniques.
counterfactuals.output:
These artists generally recommend choosing lipstick by **undertone and desired effect**, rather than following rigid skin-color rules.

| Makeup artist | Recommendations by skin tone | Occasion | Favorite/representative products | Application technique |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Carmindy** | **Fair:** sheer pink, peach, light coral, or blue-red. **Medium/olive:** rose, warm coral, brick, or true red. **Deep:** rich berry, burgundy, plum, raisin, or deep red. She cautions against very pale, chalky “nudes”; a nude should retain some pink, peach, or caramel. | For daytime, use a sheer or softly blotted version of the shade. At night, intensify it with a stronger red, berry, or gloss. | **Sally Hansen Natural Beauty Inspired by Carmindy Color Comfort Lip Color**, the lipstick range she helped create; she has also favored sheer tinted gloss for easy daytime wear. | Smooth and moisturize the lips first. For a natural result, press color on with a fingertip and blot. For a polished red lip, outline after applying lipstick—the liner corrects the edge without leaving an obvious ring. |
| **AJ Crimson** | **Fair/light:** soft nude-pink, coral, classic red, or berry. **Medium/olive:** caramel nude, terracotta, orange-red, wine, and warm berry. **Deep:** saturated orange, fuchsia, blue-red, burgundy, plum, chocolate, and caramel-based nude. His key point is that deep skin should not be limited to dark colors; vivid shades can be especially flattering. | Neutral caramel or rose works for everyday wear; orange, fuchsia, red, and wine create more impact for evening, photographs, or events. | **AJ Crimson Beauty S&M Sultry + Matte Lipstick** and the brand’s lip-gloss/lip-color collection. He is particularly associated with highly pigmented nudes, reds, oranges, and berries designed to remain vivid on deeper complexions. | Neutralize uneven lip pigmentation with a small amount of foundation or concealer, then use a lip pencil—often slightly deeper than the lipstick—to define and softly shade the corners. Apply lipstick in thin layers and blend the liner inward so there is no hard outline. |
| **Melissa Silver** | **Fair:** rosy pink, peach, coral, or cherry red. **Medium:** mauve, warm rose, brick, or true red. **Olive:** orange-red, terracotta, and warm berry. **Deep:** wine, plum, deep red, fuchsia, and rich brown-red. For nude lips, she favors a shade close to, but not lighter than, the natural lip color. | A shade one or two tones deeper than the natural lips is an easy daytime choice. For evening, she recommends a stronger red or berry; the rest of the makeup can stay restrained. | Silver has frequently worked with **Maybelline New York Color Sensational Lipcolor**; **Red Revival** is a representative classic red from the range often associated with her editorial/backstage work. | Apply color from the center of the mouth outward, then soften it with a finger or blot with tissue. For longer wear, fill in the entire lip with pencil before lipstick, apply a thin coat, blot, and reapply. Clean the perimeter with concealer for a crisp formal look. |

### Shared takeaway
- **Cool undertones:** blue-red, raspberry, mauve, plum.  
- **Warm undertones:** coral, peach, brick, terracotta, orange-red.  
- **Neutral undertones:** usually suit both groups.  
- **Day:** sheer, blotted, or close to the natural lip color.  
- **Evening:** more pigment, sharper definition, and richer red, berry, or wine tones.

Some of the older Sally Hansen, AJ Crimson, and Maybelline shades may have been renamed or discontinued, but the color families and techniques remain applicable.
